recall.question: What is the BPE intuition?
recall.answer: Start from tiny pieces (bytes or characters). Repeatedly add a token for the most frequent adjacent pair. Common strings become single tokens, rare words still split into pieces.

recall.question: What breaks when train and serve tokenizers differ?
recall.answer: Token ids shift meaning and the learned embeddings misalign. Silent and catastrophic.

sections.title: SL-02: Autoregressive factorization and the loss

keyTerms.definition: p(x_1..x_T) factored by the chain rule into per-position conditionals.
(1/T) sum_t l_ce(f_theta(x_{<t}), x_t): maximum likelihood normalized by length.
The rule factoring the joint into conditionals.

recall.question: What is the autoregressive factorization?
recall.answer: p(x_1, ..., x_T) = p(x_1) p(x_2 | x_1) ... p(x_T | x_1, ..., x_{T-1}). Each conditional has support |V|.

recall.question: What is the mental model of next-token training?
recall.answer: Every position is a classification problem with |V| classes, and the label is free: it is the next token. One document yields T training examples.

recall.question: What goes wrong packing documents without boundaries?
recall.answer: The model learns to continue across document boundaries and blends unrelated contexts.

keyTerms.definition: f_theta mapping embedding sequences to logit vectors.
Layer norm before attention and the MLP.
M_{t,j} = 0 for j <= t, -inf after: no future visibility.

recall.question: What does a transformer block contain?
recall.answer: Multi-head self-attention and position-wise MLPs (GELU or SwiGLU). Modern LLMs use PreNorm, usually with RMSNorm. Attention is the only cross-position mixing.

recall.question: What happens if you forget the causal mask in training?
recall.answer: The model reads the answer from the future, training loss collapses to near zero, and the model is useless at generation.

keyTerms.definition: Queries ask, keys advertise, values carry the payload.
c = sqrt(d_h): keeps logit variance near 1.
M_{t,j} = 0 for j <= t, -inf for j > t, added before softmax.

recall.question: Why divide by sqrt(d_h)?
recall.answer: At initialization, q and k dot products have variance d_h. Without scaling, logits grow with head dimension and the softmax saturates (tiny gradients). Dividing keeps logit variance near 1.

recall.question: What does the causal mask do?
recall.answer: M_{t,j} = 0 for j <= t, -infinity for j > t, added before the softmax: probabilities of future positions are exactly zero.

recall.question: What goes wrong applying the mask after softmax?
recall.answer: The -infinity never enters the normalization and future positions leak.

keyTerms.definition: Stores K_{1:t} and V_{1:t} across generation steps.
n_h heads in parallel, outputs concatenated and projected.
Streams the score matrix for O(T) memory.

recall.question: What is the KV cache?
recall.answer: Stores K_{1:t} and V_{1:t} so prefix keys/values are not recomputed each generation step. New rows append, old rows never recompute.

recall.question: In the 4096 example, how big is the cache?
recall.answer: T = 8192: 128.0 MiB per layer. At 32 layers: 4.0 GiB for one sequence.

recall.question: What is the main difficulty past 10K tokens?
recall.answer: Attention compute is quadratic in T: O(T^2 d). FlashAttention streams the score matrix for O(T) memory.

keyTerms.definition: Many query heads share one key/value head.
Query groups share one key/value head each; n_g between 1 and n_h.
Each token attends only to the last w tokens.
Normalize q and k before the dot product.

recall.question: What is the MQA-GQA-MHA spectrum?
recall.answer: MQA: many query heads share one key/value head. GQA: groups share one key/value head each. MHA is n_g = n_h, MQA is n_g = 1. Fewer KV heads, smaller cache: quality vs decoding efficiency.

recall.question: How does the cache scale?
recall.answer: With n_g, not n_h: MHA 128.0 MiB, GQA (n_g=8) 32.0 MiB, MQA 4.0 MiB per layer at T=8192.

recall.question: When does aggressive MQA hurt?
recall.answer: On quality-sensitive tasks: the shared key head bottlenecks distinct query behaviors and quality drops.

keyTerms.definition: Sparse layers routing tokens to expert MLPs.
The tiny classifier choosing experts per token.
The small chosen expert set per token.

recall.question: What is the MoE idea?
recall.answer: Each token consults a few specialists. Total parameters grow with m, per-token compute grows with k. The router is a tiny classifier: which experts fit this token?

recall.question: What is router collapse?
recall.answer: Every token routes to the same few experts and the rest starve. Load-balancing losses prevent it.

keyTerms.definition: Concatenate labeled examples and the test input; generate the continuation.
No examples, just a task description; no gradient updates.
Update parameters on prompt-completion pairs.
0 on prompt tokens, 1 on answer tokens.

recall.question: What changes in prompting versus SFT?
recall.answer: Prompting (ICL, zero-shot) changes the text, not the weights. SFT changes the weights: it teaches p(y | x). The loss mask is the key detail: the model learns to produce answers, not predict prompts.

recall.question: What is the SFT loss?
recall.answer: min_theta -(1/n) sum_i sum_t log p_theta(y_t^(i) | x^(i), y_{<t}^(i)), with the loss mask 0 on prompt tokens, 1 on answer tokens.

recall.question: What is format overfitting in SFT?
recall.answer: SFT on a narrow answer style: the model learns the format but forgets the pretraining distribution. Mix SFT data with pretraining-style data.

sections.title: SL-09: Train/infer mismatch and resource accounting

keyTerms.definition: The model never saw its own mistakes during training; errors compound.
Training on ground-truth prefixes.
Keep the top tokens totaling probability 0.9, renormalize.

recall.question: What is the train/infer mismatch?
recall.answer: Training feeds ground-truth prefixes (teacher forcing). Inference feeds the model's own outputs. Errors compound: a small early mistake shifts the whole continuation distribution.

recall.question: In the temperature example, what does tau do?
What is the deployment ledger?
recall.answer: Model weights, KV cache per concurrent sequence (grows with T and batch), compute per token (T^2 prefill, T per decode step).
